schema_note: Each entry: id, title, class, severity, status (open|fixed|needs-reverification|accepted-risk), location, discovered_pass, fixed_pass, verification_method, notes. Update entries in place across sessions. Do not create a second ledger file - this is the single source of truth.

stack_migration.scope: dubbing service + dashboard only - Medusa keeps its own Postgres unless told otherwise
stack_migration.confirmed_architecture: Two entry points reach Convex: (1) browser -> FastAPI (Clerk JWT -> org_xxx claim -> _resolve_legacy_workspace_id) -> Convex, and (2) RunPod worker -> FastAPI's internalJobs router (main.py:390, INTERNAL_API_KEY-gated) -> Convex. Convex itself checks identity on nothing - FastAPI is the sole trust boundary on both paths. See PIRD-001 (browser path resolution chain, needs a test) and PIRD-017 (internalJobs path, confirmed current gap).
stack_migration.note: Any finding whose status was tied to Supabase/FastAPI-era code should not be trusted at face value until re-verified against the current implementation. A status of fixed against code that no longer exists is not fixed.

findings.title: Cross-tenant workspace isolation - browser-facing resolution chain
findings.location: FastAPI: Clerk JWT -> org_xxx claim -> _resolve_legacy_workspace_id -> Convex by_workspace_id filter
findings.discovered_pass: found across roughly 6 manual passes before pass-1 (Supabase era); re-scoped pass-9
findings.notes: Confirmed architecture: Convex does not independently check identity - isolation rides entirely on FastAPI always resolving the correct workspace_id for the correct caller. Two things need an actual test, not a read-through: (1) two real tenants each only ever see their own data through every browser-facing route; (2) _resolve_legacy_workspace_id's behavior on an org_xxx with no mapped legacy workspace - current understanding is it falls through and Convex returns empty (no workspace has that legacyId), which is safe by coincidence of index semantics, not by an explicit check. Verify this is actually true and that no legacyId could ever collide with a raw org_xxx string. See scripts/workspace_isolation_test_template.py.

findings.title: update_chunk workspace-reassignment privilege escalation
findings.location: update_chunk handler - confirm which entry point owns this now (browser-facing FastAPI, or the internalJobs router)
findings.notes: Not yet re-confirmed against the current architecture. If update_chunk is reachable via the internalJobs router (the RunPod-worker path) rather than only the browser-facing path, it inherits the exact same risk as PIRD-017 - check which entry point actually owns this call before treating it as separately fixed or separately broken.

findings.title: Prompt injection into kurdish_raw reaches the dashboard render
findings.location: dubbing pipeline: transcription ingestion -> state (now Convex) -> React dashboard
findings.notes: Pass-5 closed the JS-execution/XSS vector on render. Pass-7 fenced the LLM prompt but not the input, so a poisoned first-chunk transcript can still inject text that flows downstream. Unaffected in substance by the DB/auth swap - confirm the sanitization step still runs on whatever now writes transcripts into Convex.

findings.notes: Not affected by the Convex/Clerk migration. Re-verify it blocks private/link-local ranges and cloud metadata IPs (169.254.169.254), and re-resolves the host at request time (DNS rebinding).

findings.title: Secrets stored in plaintext .env/.env.production, no secrets manager
findings.location: .env, .env.production - now also holding CLERK_SECRET_KEY, Convex deploy credentials, and INTERNAL_API_KEY
findings.notes: If Supabase is being fully retired, rotate/revoke SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY and SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET rather than leaving them live-but-unused - an unused-but-valid credential is still a live attack surface. INTERNAL_API_KEY specifically deserves extra scrutiny now: per PIRD-017, holding this one flat secret plus a forged workspace_id is enough to act as any tenant.

findings.title: user.role field exists but is never enforced
findings.notes: Watch for this exact mistake reappearing under the new stack: Clerk ships real RBAC via Organizations (membership, roles, audit logging). The lazy migration path keeps a dead role field and populates it from a Clerk claim instead of a Supabase one, still checking nothing. Either wire real role checks against Clerk Organization roles, or remove the field.

findings.location: voice upload flow; account management (missing entirely)

findings.notes: Not affected by the Convex/Clerk migration - the raw audio was never planned to live in Convex. R2 has encryption at rest by default; local FS intermediates still don't, and worker-container filesystem permissions still haven't been confirmed tight.

findings.title: Convex functions are public-callable by default - sweep required for missing per-function auth checks
findings.verification_method: scripts/convex_function_audit.sh - only users, dubbingJobs:list*, and ttsVoices:list have been spot-checked so far
findings.notes: Confirmed: every public Convex function in this codebase has zero identity checks by design - Convex is a pass-through persistence layer, FastAPI is the sole trust boundary. This is coherent IF (a) every tenant-scoped table's functions are internal* (platform-blocked from external callers, not just convention-blocked), and (b) nothing tenant-scoped is exposed as a plain public query/mutation the way ttsVoices:list intentionally is for non-tenant data (PIRD-018). Neither is confirmed for the full schema yet - run the sweep against the real convex/ directory before assuming coverage. Severity held at High rather than Critical because the spot-checked functions do follow the internal* pattern correctly; this tracks the remaining unconfirmed surface, not a confirmed hole.

findings.title: Clerk publishable-key env-var prefix mismatch risk in the Vite dashboard
findings.location: dubbing dashboard (Vite) .env - needs VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, not NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY (that prefix is for the Next.js storefront only)
findings.verification_method: scripts/env_config_lint.sh checks which prefix is present and warns if the wrong one is set for a Vite app
findings.notes: Vite only exposes client-side env vars prefixed VITE_. Copying a Next.js Clerk tutorial's env var name into the dashboard's .env means the publishable key silently never reaches the client - low severity by itself, but worth catching before someone 'fixes' the resulting auth failure by loosening something else instead of renaming the variable.

findings.title: internalJobs router trusts client-supplied workspace_id instead of deriving it from a verified source
findings.verification_method: scripts/workspace_isolation_test_template.py::test_internal_jobs_rejects_mismatched_workspace - written to currently FAIL, documenting the gap
findings.notes: This is the actual, current isolation gap - not Convex. The internalJobs router accepts workspace_id from the request body. Anyone holding the single static INTERNAL_API_KEY (which gates every cross-service call, not scoped per caller) can supply any workspace_id and read or write that tenant's data, since Convex trusts whatever string it's handed. Hardening Convex itself does not fix this - the caller constructing the malicious request would just forge whatever Convex-side check was added too. The fix is on the FastAPI side: derive workspace_id server-side from the job_id's own record (created earlier via an authenticated, JWT-verified browser request), instead of accepting it as a caller-supplied parameter. If the worker needs to reference a job, let it pass job_id only - never let it also assert which tenant that job belongs to.

findings.title: ttsVoices:list is a public, non-tenant-scoped Convex query reachable directly via HTTP
findings.verification_method: manual - confirmed voices are global reference data, not tenant-scoped
findings.notes: Deliberate design choice, not a gap: this table isn't tenant-scoped, so global read access via direct Convex HTTP access is intentional. Documented so a future pass doesn't re-flag it as an isolation bypass, and so a future 'fix' doesn't accidentally break it by adding workspace filtering that shouldn't be there.
